intro.note: Answer each question in your workbook. Show your working.
methodSteps: 1  Find the percentage of the original value
commonMistakes: Dividing by the NEW value — always divide by the ORIGINAL.
Adding the percentage of the wrong amount.
20% increase → new value is 120% of original, not 20% of original.
15% off then 15% on does NOT get back to the start.
workedExample: A coat costs £80, reduced by 15%. Find the sale price.
intro.visualAid: Bar model: Full bar = original amount (100%). Shaded portion = percentage kept. Unshaded portion = amount removed. Formula: Percentage change = (change ÷ original) × 100.

questions.content: Increase: a) £40 by 10%  b) £60 by 25%  c) £200 by 50%
Decrease: a) £80 by 20%  b) £150 by 10%  c) £500 by 35%
TV price rises from £450 to £495. a) How much increase? b) Percentage increase?
Bicycle £320, 15% off. a) Discount? b) Sale price? c) +15% back on — is it £320? Explain.
Factory: Jan 250 units, Feb 300 units. Calculate percentage increase.
Mo: buys £60, sells £78. Abi: buys £45, sells £54. a) Mo's % profit. b) Abi's %. c) Who did better?
House £200k. +12% Year 1, −8% Year 2. a) Value after Y1? b) After Y2? c) Overall % change?
